_readme: The inn, and the first conversation that takes money. The shape is the genre's: a
greeting, the price said OUT LOUD, a yes and a no - and a refusal in the keeper's own
words when the purse is short.
The yes carries spend_gold, rest and poor_next together. All three are one decision:
the runner checks the purse before collecting anything, so a night nobody can afford
costs nothing and heals nothing, and the player is told which.
poor_next is REQUIRED on a choice that charges - the build refuses a keeper who takes
money and says nothing when they cannot have it.
Four gold is exactly what one slink drops, which is the whole economy in one line: an ambient fight pays for the night it costs you.
The line after the yes is a GOING-TO-BED line, not a good-morning one, and that ordering
is forced rather than chosen: a conversation's effects are applied when it CLOSES, so
everything on this chain is said while the player is still standing there awake. The
night comes after the last word. A 'Morning already' here read as waking up before going

greet.speaker: Innkeeper
greet.text:
Room's yours for four gold.
Bed's warm and the door bolts.

poor.speaker: Innkeeper
poor.text:
Four gold, I said. Come back
when your purse agrees.

abed.speaker: Innkeeper
abed.text:
Bed's the one by the window.
Sleep well.
